opening.text: When a fire breaks out in a small town, the neighbors line up. They pass buckets from hand to hand, from the well to the flames. No one carries a bucket the whole way. Each person does one small part. The fire goes out because everyone did their small part. Service works like that.

mainMessage.text: Service is one hand passing help to the next. Small acts, done together, bless many lives.

blocks.text: **A blessing to serve** It is easy to think of service as a duty. It is also a gift.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
The opportunity to serve is one of the great blessings of membership in the Church.
It is a blessing.
**Serving without a spotlight** The person in the middle of the line isn't looking for credit. They are looking at the next hand.
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
True Christlike service is selfless and focuses on others.
Look at the next hand.
**Seeing who needs a bucket** A bucket brigade starts with someone who notices the fire. Service starts with noticing.
Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
Sister Linda K. Burton, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “First Observe, Then Serve” from the October 2012 general conference.
Observing and then serving is not always convenient and doesn’t always fit our own timetable.
Notice, then help.
**What passes back to us** The bucket that goes from hand to hand also warms the hand that holds it. Serving brings us closer to God.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
As we serve, we draw closer to God.
We draw closer to God.
**Every spot in the line matters** A line with a gap won't move the water. Everyone is needed.
And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
Every member is needed, and every member needs an opportunity to serve.
Everyone has a place.
**We are the hands** The Lord's work needs real hands. He asks us to be them.
Wherefore, be faithful; stand in the office which I have appointed unto you; succor the weak, lift up the hands which hang down, and strengthen the feeble knees.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
For now, He asks us to be His hands.
Be His hands.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they served someone, or when someone served them. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Dorcas and the coats

blocks.text: A woman named Dorcas lived in Joppa. She spent her days helping others. When she died, the widows she had helped gathered around her.

Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did. Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.
Dorcas didn't lead a movement. She made coats and gave them away. Those small acts were what people remembered.

application.text: First, think of one person who may need help this week. Second, choose one small act, like a meal, a ride or a call. Third, do it before the week ends.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know service brings us closer to God. I know small acts matter to Him. I know Jesus Christ served everyone He met. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: One candle can light a thousand others. It loses nothing. The first flame stays just as bright. Service is like that. When we give someone our time or our help, we don't run out. Often we find our own light growing.

mainMessage.text: Service is light passed from one candle to the next. Giving doesn't make us smaller.

blocks.text: **The gift of a flame** A candle is made to be shared. We are given our days and talents the same way.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
The opportunity to serve is one of the great blessings of membership in the Church.
The chance to share is a gift.
**Light that doesn't look at itself** A candle doesn't light another to be admired. It simply passes the flame.
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
True Christlike service is selfless and focuses on others.
Pass it without fuss.
**Finding the dark corners** A candle goes where the dark is. We have to notice who is sitting in the dark.
Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
Sister Linda K. Burton, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “First Observe, Then Serve” from the October 2012 general conference.
Observing and then serving is not always convenient and doesn’t always fit our own timetable.
Go where it is dark.
**A brighter room** When two candles stand together, the room is brighter for both. Serving lifts the one serving as well.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
As we serve, we draw closer to God.
The room gets brighter.
**Every candle counts** A small flame matters in a dark room. No one is too small to serve.
And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
Every member is needed, and every member needs an opportunity to serve.
Every flame counts.
**Carried by the Lord's hands** The flame passes through hands. The Lord's work is done by willing hands.
Wherefore, be faithful; stand in the office which I have appointed unto you; succor the weak, lift up the hands which hang down, and strengthen the feeble knees.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
For now, He asks us to be His hands.
Hold out your hands.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when a small act of service lit something bigger. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Savior washes feet

blocks.text: On His last evening with His disciples, Jesus Christ knelt and washed their feet. It was a servant's job.
If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.
The Lord of all knelt. He showed that no service is beneath us. Then He asked us to do the same.

application.text: First, think of a place in your life where someone seems to be in the dark. Second, find one way to bring them light. Third, don't wait to be asked.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know service lights the lives of others and my own. I know the Savior gave us the example. I know Jesus Christ is the Light of the World. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: In a dry village, a well is the heart of the place. People come with jars. The well doesn't ask who they are. It gives water. And a good well is fed by springs below that never stop. Service is like drawing from that well. We share what we have been given, and God keeps the spring flowing.

mainMessage.text: Service is sharing the water we have been given. God keeps the well full.

blocks.text: **The well is for sharing** A well that no one draws from is wasted. Our time and talents are meant to be used for others.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
The opportunity to serve is one of the great blessings of membership in the Church.
Sharing is a blessing.
**The well doesn't ask for thanks** Water flows without a speech. Real service does too.
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
True Christlike service is selfless and focuses on others.
Give freely.
**Seeing the thirsty** A well can only help the people who come. We can go to the ones who can't. That means seeing them first.
Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
Sister Linda K. Burton, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “First Observe, Then Serve” from the October 2012 general conference.
Observing and then serving is not always convenient and doesn’t always fit our own timetable.
Go to the thirsty.
**Drawn closer to the spring** The more we draw, the closer we come to the source. Serving brings us nearer to God.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
As we serve, we draw closer to God.
Closer to the spring.
**Many jars, one well** The village needs many people to carry water. Every person has a part.
And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
Every member is needed, and every member needs an opportunity to serve.
Everyone carries a jar.
**His hands, our hands** The Lord gives the water. We carry it. He asks us to be His hands.
Wherefore, be faithful; stand in the office which I have appointed unto you; succor the weak, lift up the hands which hang down, and strengthen the feeble knees.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
For now, He asks us to be His hands.
Carry the water.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone stopped to help them, or when they stopped for someone else. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: The Good Samaritan

blocks.text: A man was beaten and left on the road. Others passed by. One man stopped.

But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The Samaritan saw, felt and acted. He gave his time, his oil and his own ride. That is service from start to finish.

application.text: First, ask yourself who in your life might be thirsty for kindness. Second, go to them, not the other way around. Third, give without waiting to be asked.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know God fills the well when we share. I know every person we help is dear to Him. I know Jesus Christ is the Living Water. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: In a rowing boat, eight people pull on eight oars. No one gets a medal for rowing alone. The boat only moves when everyone pulls together. The person who rows hardest and quietest often matters most. Service is like rowing. It takes many people, pulling in one direction.

mainMessage.text: Service is rowing together. Every oar matters, and the boat moves when we pull as one.

blocks.text: **A privilege to row** It is an honor to be in the boat. Serving is a chance, not a chore.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
The opportunity to serve is one of the great blessings of membership in the Church.
It is an honor.
**Rowing, not showing off** A good rower doesn't look to the crowd. They keep their eyes on the others in the boat.
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
True Christlike service is selfless and focuses on others.
Keep eyes on the boat.
**Seeing who is slipping behind** The good rower notices when a partner is tiring. Service means seeing who needs help, even when it is not our time.
Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
Sister Linda K. Burton, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “First Observe, Then Serve” from the October 2012 general conference.
Observing and then serving is not always convenient and doesn’t always fit our own timetable.
See who is tiring.
**The same shore** The boat gets us all to the same shore. When we serve, we draw closer to God and to each other.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
As we serve, we draw closer to God.
The shore is nearer.
**Every seat is filled** An empty seat slows the boat. Each person is needed.
And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
Every member is needed, and every member needs an opportunity to serve.
Take your seat.
**The Lord at the helm** Someone steers the boat. The Lord guides, and we supply the strength of our arms.
Wherefore, be faithful; stand in the office which I have appointed unto you; succor the weak, lift up the hands which hang down, and strengthen the feeble knees.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
For now, He asks us to be His hands.
Pull the oar.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when they served alongside others on a shared task. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Ammon the servant

blocks.text: Ammon was a prince's son, but he went to the Lamanites as a missionary. When he was offered a high place, he chose a humble one.

But Ammon said unto him: Nay, but I will be thy servant. Therefore Ammon became a servant to king Lamoni. And it came to pass that he was set among other servants to watch the flocks of Lamoni, according to the custom of the Lamanites.
Ammon took the lowest seat in the boat. His faithful service opened the king's heart. Humble work can open great doors.

application.text: First, find a group effort in your ward, family or neighborhood. Second, show up and take a small job. Third, row with a glad heart.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know service is stronger when we do it together. I know God honors humble work. I know Jesus Christ served at the lowest seat for us all. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

opening.text: A quilt is made of many pieces. Some are bright. Some are plain. Alone, each piece is just a scrap of cloth. Stitched together, they make something warm that covers a whole family. Service is how we stitch. Each small act joins one life to another.

mainMessage.text: Service stitches lives together. Many small acts make something that warms everyone.

blocks.text: **A gift to stitch** It is a joy to add a piece to the quilt. Serving is a gift we get to give.
And behold, I tell you these things that ye may learn wisdom; that ye may learn that when ye are in the service of your fellow beings ye are only in the service of your God.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
The opportunity to serve is one of the great blessings of membership in the Church.
It is a joy to give.
**Stitching for the cover, not the credit** No one signs each stitch. The quilt is the point, not the quilter.
For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
True Christlike service is selfless and focuses on others.
The quilt is the point.
**Finding the cold spot** A quilt is made for someone who is cold. We have to notice who is cold.
Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
Sister Linda K. Burton, Relief Society General President, said this in her talk “First Observe, Then Serve” from the October 2012 general conference.
Observing and then serving is not always convenient and doesn’t always fit our own timetable.
Notice who is cold.
**Warmed ourselves** The one who stitches is warmed by the work. As we serve, we draw closer to God.
And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
As we serve, we draw closer to God.
The stitcher is warmed too.
**Every piece belongs** No piece is left out. Even a small, plain scrap holds the pattern together.
And the eye cannot say unto the hand, I have no need of thee: nor again the head to the feet, I have no need of you.
Elder Carl B. Cook of the Seventy said this in his talk “Serve” from the October 2016 general conference.
Every member is needed, and every member needs an opportunity to serve.
Every piece belongs.
**Hands that hold the needle** The Lord's work still needs hands. He asks us to be His hands.
Wherefore, be faithful; stand in the office which I have appointed unto you; succor the weak, lift up the hands which hang down, and strengthen the feeble knees.
Sister Cheryl A. Esplin, First Counselor in the Primary General Presidency, said this in her talk “He Asks Us to Be His Hands” from the April 2016 general conference.
For now, He asks us to be His hands.
Take up the needle.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time when someone served them after a hard moment, or when they did the same for another. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: Peter's mother-in-law serves

blocks.text: Peter's mother-in-law lay sick with a fever. Jesus Christ came to her.
And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.
The Savior lifted her. The first thing she did when she was well was to serve. Service is often how we say thank you for being lifted.

application.text: First, think of a time someone lifted you. Second, pass it on this week to one person. Third, keep a list of small acts you have done, and add one new one each week.

testimony.prompt: The member adds their own words. Lines the app offers:

blocks.text: I know serving others is how we thank God. I know He sees every small stitch. I know Jesus Christ lifts us so that we may lift others. I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.
